Example data: a breast cancer risk model and validation studies

Source: R/data.R
bc_data.Rd

Example inputs for computeAbsoluteRisk(), computeAbsoluteRiskSplitInterval(), ModelValidation() and plotModelValidation(): a breast cancer relative-risk model with 13 risk factors and 72 SNPs, a reference dataset, incidence and mortality rates, profiles to apply the model to, and simulated studies to validate it. Load them all with data(bc_data, package = "iCARE").

Format

The model

  • bc_model_formula: formula of the relative-risk model, with the 13 risk factors below and an interaction of HRT use with body mass index.

  • bc_model_cov_info: list describing each risk factor: its name, its type ("continuous" or "factor"), and for factors the levels and the reference level.

  • bc_model_log_or: named vector of the 77 log odds ratios of the model, one per column of its design matrix.

  • bc_model_log_or_post_50: the log odds ratios for women aged 50 years or older (an example for computeAbsoluteRiskSplitInterval()).

  • bc_72_snps: data frame of 72 breast cancer SNPs with columns snp.name, snp.odds.ratio (per-allele odds ratio) and snp.freq (risk-allele frequency), from Michailidou et al. (2017).

The population

  • ref_cov_dat: data frame of the 13 risk factors in 14,137 women, representative of the US population (imputed from NHIS 2010 and NHANES; references 4 and 5).

  • ref_cov_dat_post_50: the reference dataset for women aged 50 years or older.

  • bc_inc: matrix of the annual breast cancer incidence rates by single year of age (columns: age, rate) from SEER (reference 3).

  • mort_inc: matrix of the annual mortality rates from causes other than breast cancer by single year of age (columns: age, rate) from CDC WONDER (reference 1).

Profiles

  • new_cov_prof: data frame of the risk factors of three women.

  • new_snp_prof: data frame of the genotypes (risk-allele counts) of the 72 SNPs of the same three women; NA marks a missing genotype.

Validation studies

  • validation.cohort.data: simulated full cohort of 50,000 women with the columns

    • id: subject identifier;

    • the 13 risk factors: famhist (family history of breast cancer in a first-degree relative), menarche_dec, parity, birth_dec, agemeno_dec, height_dec, bmi_dec (categories of age at menarche, number of births, age at first birth, age at menopause, height and body mass index), rd_menohrt (menopausal status and HRT use), rd2_everhrt_e, rd2_everhrt_c, rd2_currhrt (ever use of estrogen-only or combined HRT, current HRT use), alcoholdweek_dec (categories of drinks per week) and ever_smoke;

    • study.entry.age, study.exit.age: ages at entry and exit;

    • observed.outcome: 1 if breast cancer developed during follow-up;

    • time.of.onset: years from entry to onset (Inf without onset);

    • observed.followup: years of follow-up;

    • inclusion: 0 (a placeholder for the indicator of inclusion in the nested case-control study; see the examples).

  • validation.nested.case.control.data: a simulated case-control study of 5,285 women nested in the cohort, with the same columns and the 72 SNP genotypes (columns named by the SNPs' rs identifiers).

  • output: a result of computeAbsoluteRisk() from an earlier version of iCARE.

References

  1. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS). Underlying Cause of Death 1999-2011 on CDC WONDER Online Database, released 2014.

  2. Michailidou K, Beesley J, Lindstrom S, et al. (2015). Genome-wide association analysis of more than 120,000 individuals identifies 15 new susceptibility loci for breast cancer. Nature Genetics 47: 373-380.

  3. Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program SEER*Stat Database: Incidence - SEER 18 Regs Research Data, Nov 2011 Sub. National Cancer Institute.

  4. 2010 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) Public Use Data Release. National Center for Health Statistics, 2011.

  5. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey Questionnaire. National Center for Health Statistics, 2010.

  6. Michailidou K, Lindstrom S, Dennis J, et al. (2017). Association analysis identifies 65 new breast cancer risk loci. Nature 551: 92-94.

Examples

data(bc_data, package = "iCARE")
bc_model_formula
#> diagnosis ~ famhist + as.factor(menarche_dec) + as.factor(parity) + 
#>     as.factor(birth_dec) + as.factor(agemeno_dec) + as.factor(height_dec) + 
#>     as.factor(bmi_dec) + as.factor(rd_menohrt) + rd2_everhrt_e + 
#>     rd2_everhrt_c + rd2_currhrt + as.factor(alcoholdweek_dec) + 
#>     as.factor(ever_smoke) + as.factor(rd_menohrt) * as.factor(bmi_dec)
head(bc_inc)
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    0    0
#> [2,]    1    0
#> [3,]    2    0
#> [4,]    3    0
#> [5,]    4    0
#> [6,]    5    0
head(bc_72_snps)
#>     snp.name snp.odds.ratio snp.freq
#> 1   rs616488           0.94     0.33
#> 2 rs11552449           1.04     0.17
#> 3 rs11249433           1.11     0.41
#> 4 rs12405132           0.97     0.37
#> 5 rs12048493           1.04     0.38
#> 6  rs6678914           1.00     0.41

# Inclusion probabilities of the nested case-control study, estimated from
# the cohort by logistic regression (as in the vignette)
cohort <- validation.cohort.data
ncc <- validation.nested.case.control.data
cohort$inclusion <- as.numeric(cohort$id %in% ncc$id)
selection <- glm(
  inclusion ~ observed.outcome * (study.entry.age + observed.followup),
  data = cohort, family = binomial
)
probability <- fitted(selection)[match(ncc$id, cohort$id)]
summary(probability)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#> 0.03008 0.07612 0.10964 0.24876 0.17982 0.86280
